findings.issue: The full-source hashes are byte-identical within each group. Choosing Shabbat, or Sepharad over Ashkenaz, changes nothing in the compiled output. That is what the index predicts: no morning content is gated on Shabbat, every Shabbat-gated section sits behind a Maariv gate, and no condition uses a broad rite. So the identical hashes confirm that Sepharad/Ashkenaz is independent of the German choice. They also mean the two Shabbat cases add no evidence about Shabbat content in the morning, because there is none to test.
findings.recommendation: No change. Recorded so nobody reads the Shabbat cases as testing more than they do.

findings.issue: The Minchah compile contains only the entering-synagogue verses (shaharit=false gate) and the ungated Psalm 24 appendix. It has no Ashrei and no Amidah, because the weekday Minchah section is gated on 29 Elul, not Shabbat, not yom tov. This proves that no morning unit leaks into Minchah. It does not show the Minchah section itself compiling.
findings.recommendation: Outside this change. If wanted, add a Minchah case dated 29 Elul so the section is actually active.

findings.issue: The HTML proof is a summary of three rite cases (german, other, unknown), not eight. It has no separate field for CSS hiding of condition labels when the condition is true. I could check its stated results (copies per unit 1/1/2, Neshamah before or after the block, four bilingual labels) against the compiled XML, and they match. I could not inspect the DOM or CSS myself.
findings.recommendation: No change needed for approval. If the CSS-hiding claim should be on record, add an explicit field to the report.

Numbers 6:24-26 has a chapter milestone and verse milestones 24, 25 and 26 with matching @corresp in both languages, in all six morning excerpts. In unknown it appears twice, once in each alternative, both complete.

Ellu Devarim is complete in both languages in every copy. Hebrew ends וְתַלְמוּד תּוֹרָה כְּנֶגֶד כֻּלָּם, English ends 'with the study of Torah outweighing all of them.' The human-confirmed וְהָרַאְיוֹן is kept exactly as written in every copy.

Every unit resolves to paired items, he = prayerbook_for_the_new_year-heidenheim-1965-he and en = prayerbook_for_the_new_year-marmorstein-1965-en. The facs and pb references are unchanged (n43/n44, n45/n46, pb n=5 in Vehaarev; Barukh Sheamar n59/n60).

All four labels are bilingual, with tei:foreign xml:lang='he' followed by xml:lang='en', in the same pattern as the minyan, Shabbat and festival labels (index.xml:1237, 1253, 1273, 1291; unknown:194, 232, 381, 418). They are the conditionals' own instructions, not tei:head, and none appears in any definite-rite output.
In definite rites each unit's @corresp appears once. In unknown the Neshamah and the five units each appear twice, which the alternatives require. Only the first copy of each can be reached by URN.
